title: Iowa Ranks 7th for Alien Abduction Odds, Plus 5 Wild UFO Tales
excerpt: A new study puts Iowa seventh for estimated alien abduction odds. Plus, discover five strange UFO reports from across Iowa.
content:
Aliens, extraterrestrials, visitors from another world, little green men... whatever you call them, they're a popular topic around Halloween. According to a new study, Iowa is one of the states where people report some pretty strange encounters and, apparently, even have a pretty good chance of being abducted.

Get our free mobile app

A study from Canada Sports Betting ranks Iowa seventh in the country for estimated alien abduction odds. Researchers analyzed UFO reports and identified accounts involving possible abductions, physical contact, or unexplained missing time. The study estimates that Iowa has 3.70 abduction-flagged reports per million residents, with lifetime odds of about one in 17,000. It also counted 162 UFO sightings in Iowa between 2020 and 2024.

That's quite a few reports about the little green men from Mars. Need more proof that Iowa has its fair share of strange alien stories? Here are five unusual cases that might make you think twice before looking up at that glowing orb in the night sky.

1. The Council Bluffs Couple Who Reported Missing Time

One of Iowa's stranger alleged encounters reportedly happened in Council Bluffs in 1947. According to the story, a young couple saw a large disc-shaped object with flashing red lights near Big Lake Park. The pair watched as the object hovered near a tree and directed a beam of light toward them. The next thing they remember was driving in daylight with an unexplained gap in their memory. There's an important catch: the story's documented trail is weak. A UFO researcher notes that the account surfaced online decades after the alleged event.

2. The Mysterious Fireball in Council Bluffs

Council Bluffs makes another appearance with a much better-documented mystery. On December 17, 1977, witnesses reported a reddish object falling toward Big Lake Park, followed by a flash and what appeared to be burning or molten material on the ground. Local fire and police personnel reportedly investigated the scene. The unusual material became the center of a long-running UFO mystery, and the incident later attracted interest from UFO researchers. Was it a spacecraft, a simple piece of local industrial material, or something else? The incident remains an intriguing story in Council Bluffs, still others say hoax.

3. A Strange Encounter on a Grinnell Farm

A farmer near Grinnell reported an unusual encounter in July 1975 involving a large, illuminated rectangular object hovering above a field near a hay barn. According to the report, the object released glowing blobs of light that disappeared before reaching the ground. The witness also described an unusual sulfur-like smell and said the object seemed to move in response to his movements. An additional note said the witness held deep religious convictions, and that the interviewer believed he was very credible.

4. A Mysterious Radar Sighting at a Sioux City Air Force Base

Could the Air Force have tracked an unidentified object over Iowa traveling faster than 1,200 miles per hour? According to a submitted story that may have happened at a Sioux City Air Force base in 1954. The witness said his father, an Air Force radar technician, described a night when the base went on alert after radar reportedly detected an unknown object flying at 50,000 to 80,000 feet. The object allegedly traveled south before disappearing from the radar screen, and personnel were reportedly told to forget the incident.

5. A Report of Strange Lights and Missing Time in Dubuque

A more recent entry in the UFO-reporting archives describes an alleged encounter near a Dubuque cemetery in October 1996. The witness reported seeing an unusually bright light with several friends. The light appeared to move rapidly, and the witness described becoming unable to move before later realizing that approximately two and a half hours had passed. The report also describes a mark on the witness's body afterward.

Should Iowans Be Worried About Alien Abductions?

Really? Probably not based on these numbers; the ranking makes for an entertaining Halloween conversation, but its estimated odds shouldn't be confused with a scientifically established probability of being abducted by extraterrestrials. However, the reports show how stories about strange lights, missing time, and unexplained objects continue to capture people's imaginations. Even if you don't believe in them, the people who made the reports do.

Here's the deal, if you find yourself outside this Halloween and spot something unusual in the Iowa sky, take a closer look. Remember that an unidentified object is most likely NOT an alien spacecraft. However, if you DO happen to lose a couple of hours while staring at the stars; you may just have a story for next Halloween.

LOOK: The states with the most UFO sightings

For each state, we’ve also included details of famous UFO sightings in that state. Of note is that almost three-quarters of all UFO sighting reports in the United States occur between 4 p.m. and midnight, and tend to peak between 9 and 10 p.m. Food for thought next time you're out scoping for alien life.
